title: Tune claude.md files and prompts
summary: Architecture analysis for auditing and unifying prompt systems across local orchestrator and GitHub Actions workflows, trimming CLAUDE.md token waste, and ensuring prompt appropriateness per task.

problem_statement.description: The egg platform has two parallel prompt generation systems — 7 bash scripts for GitHub Actions and 5 Python functions for the local orchestrator — that serve overlapping agent roles but were developed independently. Review criteria, autofixer rules, and contract verification logic are duplicated with subtle divergence. The monolithic CLAUDE.md (~15.5 KB) is loaded for every agent invocation regardless of task type, with ~40% of content irrelevant to most invocations.
goals: Unify prompt generators so local orchestration and GitHub Actions use the same review criteria
Trim CLAUDE.md to avoid wasting tokens on frontloaded context not relevant to the current task
Ensure each prompt is appropriate for its specific task and agent role
Eliminate duplicate and dead code in the prompt system

claude_md.assembly_method: Hardcoded rules_order list, concatenated with '---' separators, no conditional logic

rule_files.purpose: Agent role, workflow, PR lifecycle, git safety

functions.name: _build_review_prompt()
functions.purpose: Review prompts with typed verdict JSON output

slash_commands.note: Loaded on-demand when invoked, NOT frontloaded into CLAUDE.md

findings.title: Review criteria duplicated between GHA and orchestrator with divergence
findings.description: Four categories of review criteria exist in two separate implementations that overlap ~80% but differ in detail level. The GHA versions (in bash scripts) are generally more detailed than the orchestrator versions (in Python string literals).

differences: GHA adds 'Insecure cryptography or randomness' under Security
GHA adds 'Incorrect algorithm complexity for data size' under Correctness
GHA adds 'State corruption scenarios' under Robustness
GHA adds 'Missing or incorrect abstractions' under Design
GHA includes detailed 'How to Review' methodology section (5 steps)
GHA includes 'Skip' section (linter issues, type annotations, auto-generated files)
Orchestrator version has none of the above
Same 5 anti-patterns listed, nearly identical wording
GHA adds 'What to Skip' section scoping the review
GHA adds nuance: 'Small metadata and task context are fine' for pre-fetching
Orchestrator version is terse (15 lines vs 70+ lines)
GHA includes egg-contract CLI commands for marking criteria verified
Orchestrator omits the CLI verification step
GHA adds 'Missing or outdated dependencies in lock files' as auto-fixable
GHA adds 'Build failures from missing environment config' as report-only
Orchestrator has 3 categories each; GHA has 4 categories each

findings.risk: Criteria diverge over time. Updates in one place are forgotten in the other.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md includes ~6.3 KB of context irrelevant to most agent invocations
findings.description: contract.md (2.7 KB) and orchestrator.md (3.2 KB) are SDLC-specific but loaded for all agents, including ad-hoc tasks and GHA workflows. pr-descriptions.md (445 B) is only relevant during PR creation. Total irrelevant context for non-SDLC invocations: ~6.3 KB (~40% of CLAUDE.md).
findings.impact: ~1,600 tokens of cognitive noise per non-SDLC invocation. Token cost is modest, but irrelevant instructions may distract agents from task-relevant rules.
findings.mitigation: Conditional inclusion based on EGG_PIPELINE_ID environment variable in setup_agent_rules()

findings.title: Dead code in _build_phase_prompt() with identical is_local branches
findings.description: Lines 1166-1181 (refine phase) and 1196-1211 (plan phase) have if/else branches on is_local that produce identical output in both branches.

findings.title: Duplicate rule directory (claude-rules/ symlink to .claude/rules/)
findings.description: sandbox/claude-rules/ is a symlink to sandbox/.claude/rules/. The Dockerfile copies from claude-rules/ which Docker follows through the symlink. Both paths reference the same files. The symlink is confusing but functionally harmless.

findings.title: Slash commands and orchestrator agent prompts duplicate role instructions
findings.description: Slash commands (coder-mode.md, tester-mode.md, etc.) and _build_agent_prompt() both define role-specific instructions for the same agent roles. Slash commands are richer (file access constraints, handoff formats, quality checklists). The orchestrator could load these instead of maintaining separate, less detailed versions.

findings.title: Unified review criteria are phase-specific (orchestrator-only, no GHA equivalent)
findings.description: _get_unified_criteria() returns different criteria for refine, plan, and implement phases. These are orchestrator-specific (GHA has no equivalent lifecycle concept) and don't need unification. They're well-structured.

findings.title: GHA-only capabilities that appropriately have no orchestrator equivalent
findings.description: Conflict resolution (build-conflict-prompt.sh), doc-updater (build-doc-updater-prompt.sh), and the GHA-specific conventions files are PR-centric automations that don't apply to local orchestration. These are appropriately different.

recommended_approach.name: Shared markdown criteria files with conditional CLAUDE.md assembly
recommended_approach.summary: Extract duplicated review criteria into shared markdown files that both GHA bash scripts and orchestrator Python functions read at runtime. Conditionally assemble CLAUDE.md to exclude SDLC-specific sections for non-pipeline agents. Clean up dead code and eliminate the redundant claude-rules/ symlink.
rationale: Shared markdown files are the simplest unification path — both bash (cat) and Python (Path.read_text()) can read them without additional dependencies
The trusted checkout in GHA workflows already provides access to the full repo, so GHA scripts can read shared files directly
Conditional CLAUDE.md assembly is a minimal change to setup_agent_rules() that checks one environment variable (EGG_PIPELINE_ID)
The .egg/review-rules.md user-override mechanism is preserved — shared files serve as defaults, user overrides take priority
No new Python dependencies or build complexity introduced
constraints: GHA prompt scripts must run from a trusted checkout (main branch) — shared files must be available at that point
GHA and orchestrator have different output mechanisms (GitHub reviews vs JSON verdict files) — only criteria content is shared, not output format instructions
Convention files (review-conventions.md, autofixer-conventions.md, conflict-conventions.md) are GHA-specific and remain separate
CLAUDE.md must be available without repo mount — it's baked into the Docker image at build time
The .egg/review-rules.md, .egg/autofixer-rules.md, .egg/conflict-rules.md user-override mechanism must be preserved

alternatives_considered.name: Shared Python module for criteria
alternatives_considered.description: Extract criteria into a shared Python module in shared/egg_prompts/. Orchestrator imports directly; GHA scripts call a thin Python CLI.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Adds Python dependency to GHA bash scripts, increasing complexity for marginal benefit over shared markdown files

alternatives_considered.name: Move all prompt building into GHA action
alternatives_considered.description: Replace individual bash scripts with a single prompt builder in the action/ directory.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Doesn't solve duplication with orchestrator — still two systems

alternatives_considered.name: Full dynamic CLAUDE.md with role-based sections
alternatives_considered.description: Make CLAUDE.md fully dynamic based on agent role, task type, and phase.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Over-engineered for the savings. Only contract.md and orchestrator.md are conditionally relevant. Simple EGG_PIPELINE_ID check suffices.

open_questions.question: Should the .egg/review-rules.md user-override mechanism be extended to orchestrator reviews?
open_questions.context: Currently user overrides only work in GHA. The recommended approach would also apply them in the orchestrator, making behavior consistent. This seems clearly desirable but is a behavioral change.
open_questions.recommendation: Yes — extend user overrides to orchestrator. Users who customize review rules likely want them applied everywhere.

open_questions.question: Should the orchestrator load slash command files as agent prompt foundations instead of maintaining separate, less detailed role instructions?
open_questions.context: Slash commands (coder-mode.md, etc.) have richer instructions than _build_agent_prompt(). The orchestrator could load these files and append phase-specific context, eliminating another duplication source.
open_questions.recommendation: Defer to a follow-up issue. The slash commands are loaded on-demand by Claude Code and have a different format than what _build_agent_prompt() produces. Unifying them requires more design work than this issue warrants.

open_questions.question: Should the shared criteria files live in shared/prompts/ or a different location?
open_questions.context: The shared/ directory currently contains Python packages (egg_config, egg_container, etc.). Adding markdown files is a new pattern. Alternative: action/shared-criteria/ or a top-level prompts/ directory.
open_questions.recommendation: Use shared/prompts/ — it's the most natural location given the shared/ directory is explicitly for cross-component shared resources. The fact that it currently contains Python packages doesn't preclude non-Python content.

risk_assessment.risk: GHA trusted checkout won't have shared/prompts/ files
risk_assessment.mitigation: GHA workflows check out the main branch for prompt building. Shared files will be on main after the PR is merged. During rollout, GHA scripts should have a fallback to inline defaults if the shared file doesn't exist.

risk_assessment.risk: Orchestrator can't find shared/prompts/ at runtime
risk_assessment.mitigation: The orchestrator runs from the repo root. Use EGG_REPO_PATH / 'shared/prompts/' with a fallback to inline defaults.

Run existing tests before and after changes. The test files for GHA prompt builders (tests/action/) and orchestrator prompts (orchestrator/tests/test_pipeline_prompts.py) will need updates to account for shared file reads.

risk_assessment.risk: Conditional CLAUDE.md breaks agent behavior in non-SDLC mode
risk_assessment.mitigation: contract.md and orchestrator.md are SDLC-specific CLIs that non-SDLC agents never use. Removing them from non-SDLC agents has no behavioral impact.
